etymologies.etymologyHTML: By surface analysis, include +‎ -ing.

quote.citation: 2006 March 27, John Whiting (of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLC), transcribed in The 2006 Budget: Fourth Report of [United Kingdom House of Commons Treasury Committee] Session 2005-06, Volume II, →ISBN, page 20:
quote.text: I have always argued that it is one that deserves a thorough-going policy review, which might come to all sorts of conclusions, including it is doing what the Government of the day wants it to.

definitions.definition: Such as, among which; introducing one or more parts of the group or topic just mentioned.

quote.citation: 2013 August 10, “Can China clean up fast enough?”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8848:
quote.text: All this has led to an explosion of protest across China, including among a middle class that has discovered nimbyism.

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of include
